verification_report.summary: The supplement is correct conditional on analytic_approximation_01 and intrinsic_trace_data_01, whose reports were still incomplete at the final check. Their stipulated conclusions were accepted as instructed; this verdict does not certify those prerequisites. All deductions in the supplement were checked in textual order. The exact factor is 1/2: SGPT's ordered formula has coefficient 1/(n+1); for n=1 the j=0 terms cancel, while the non-pluripolar masses are A-D_u(Y) and A-D_m(Y). Ordinary equivalence of u_m|Y and w_m gives zero distance, and total-variation convergence gives the limit. The finite rational logarithmic potentials w_m satisfy SGPT's analytic-singularity definition in the fixed Kähler background A eta. Since A>D_u(Y), the target has positive mass, so the accepted analytic-closure characterization proves I-goodness on Y. For the final identification, compact Kähler X admits a closed background containing u, and SGPT's quasi-equisingular approximants of type (2^{-j}, I(2^j u)) restrict to the ordinary type of w_{2^j}. Their uniform curvature bound permits a sufficiently large common curve background B eta; the same distance calculation verifies the trace definition and hence uniqueness modulo P-equivalence. No ambient bounded-mass property or Hermitian ambient singularity metric is used. The specified local SGPT TeX statements and definitions were checked directly; arXiv theorem searches were followed by web verification. Public corroboration: [SGPT](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT2.pdf) and [The metric geometry of singularity types, Lemma 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.00839).
